Example 3
Consider the following recurrence relation.
T(n)=2T(n2)+n2T\lparen n\rparen = 2T \left( \cfrac{n}{2} \right) + n^2T(n)=2T(2n​)+n2
Let's calculate its time complexity using the master theorem.
Step 1: Compare the recurrence relation with the general form.
The general form of T(n) is:
T(n)=aT(nb)+Ө(nk(log⁡n)p)T\lparen n\rparen = aT \left( \cfrac{n}{b} \right) + Ө(n^k \lparen \log n \rparen ^p)T(n)=aT(bn​)+Ө(nk(logn)p)
Step 2: Rewrite the recurrence relation to match the general form.
T(n)=2∗T(n2)+Ө(n2(log⁡n)0)T\lparen n\rparen = 2 *T \left( \cfrac{n}{2} \right) + Ө(n^2 \lparen \log n \rparen ^0)T(n)=2∗T(2n​)+Ө(n2(logn)0)

Since a≥1a \geq 1a≥1, b > 1, k≥0k \geq 0k≥0, and p is a real number, the master theorem is possible.
